clue.text: African born in airline building

indicators.note: in tells us the born abbreviation sits inside the rebuilt airline letters
building here means constructing something new out of the letters of the word airline

parts.note: b. is the standard abbreviation for born, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone from Africa was delivered into the world inside an airline's headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' looks like a noun (the airline's offices) but is the anagram signal; the rearranged letters give LIERIAN, which 'in' opens to take B.
explanation.definitionFit: A Liberian is a native of Liberia, a country in West Africa.

clue.text: God gives up Middle East port

indicators.note: in a down clue, giving up means sending the word upwards, so the port is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Suez is the Egyptian port at the southern end of the Suez Canal

explanation.surface: A deity surrenders a harbour town in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives up' turns SUEZ round to make the answer reading downwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief of the Greek pantheon, ruler of Olympus, is a god.

clue.text: Book on game found under the table?

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the book letter comes first

parts.note: lotto is a game of chance like bingo

explanation.surface: A book is placed on top of a board game discovered beneath a table.
explanation.definitionFit: Being drunk enough to slide under the table is a jokey picture of being thoroughly intoxicated.

clue.text: Stand motionless over time

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: still means not moving
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Stand without moving for a lengthy period.
explanation.definitionFit: A stillage is a frame or platform on which goods or casks are set, a kind of stand.

clue.text: Showing wilfulness, the gods ran amok

indicators.note: running amok means going wild, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Self-willed deities charged about out of control.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone headstrong is obstinate and self-willed, determined to have their own way.

clue.text: Naturalist organised women involved in repair

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: to darn is to mend a hole in cloth
the WI, the Women's Institute, is a British organisation for women

explanation.surface: A nature expert sorted out some women who were busy with mending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised women' looks like an anagram but means WI, the Women's Institute, a British community organisation for women.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Darwin was the Victorian naturalist behind the theory of evolution.

clue.text: Defamed in song about inventor

indicators.note: about means going round, so the song word surrounds the inventor

parts.note: a lied is a German art song
Alexander Graham Bell invented the telephone

explanation.surface: Someone was slandered in a ballad about an inventor.
explanation.definitionFit: To be libelled is to have false damaging statements published about you, a form of defamation.

clue.text: Failure of half the Home Counties

parts.note: demi- is a prefix meaning half
the Home Counties surround London in the South East of England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: Half of the counties around London have collapsed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London, in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A demise is an end or downfall, the failure of an enterprise.

clue.text: The curse of an ancient city

parts.note: a ban can mean an anathema or curse, as in a church ban

explanation.surface: The curse laid on some old city.
explanation.definitionFit: Theban is the adjective for Thebes, an ancient city of Greece and of Egypt.

clue.text: Fewer praise missing bishop

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the bishop letter is dropped from the praise word

parts.note: to bless is to praise or glorify
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: Less praise is given because the bishop is absent.
explanation.definitionFit: Less is used colloquially for a smaller number, standing in for fewer.

clue.text: 'umiliated when found in urban area that's dilapidated

indicators.note: found in means located within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a town is an urban area
humiliated is humbled; with the H dropped as the apostrophe shows, it gives umbled

explanation.surface: A Cockney feels humiliated on finding themselves in a run-down part of town.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''umiliated' signals a dropped H, so HUMBLED loses its H.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbledown building is falling to pieces, which is to say dilapidated.

clue.text: Writer entertains holy man in cafe

indicators.note: to entertain is to take in as a guest, so the pen word holds the saint

parts.note: a biro is a ballpoint pen, something that writes
St is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: An author hosts a priest in a coffee shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' is a pen, not an author.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small informal restaurant, much like a cafe.

clue.text: One giving money for champers is hit of a Tory assembly

indicators.note: assembly means putting parts together, so the letters are reassembled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who funds the fizz is the star turn of a Conservative gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'champers' suggests champagne, but here it means teeth, the things that chomp. 'assembly' rearranges HIT OF A TORY.
explanation.definitionFit: The tooth fairy of nursery lore leaves coins in exchange for children's shed teeth.

clue.text: Setting out pictures in swindle

indicators.note: in places the pictures word inside the swindle word

parts.note: a sting is a confidence trick or swindle
art means paintings and pictures collectively

explanation.surface: Some paintings were set out as part of a con.
explanation.definitionFit: Starting and setting out both mean beginning a journey or undertaking.

clue.text: Where black and blue are colours and red and white are not

definitions.text: Where black and blue are colours and red and white are not

parts.words: Where black and blue are colours and red and white are not
parts.note: a game played on green baize in which the higher-value balls are called the colours, while the reds and the white cue ball are not

explanation.surface: A riddle about some colour scheme in which red and white do not count.
explanation.walkthrough: In this cue sport the reds are balls but not 'colours', and the white is the cue ball.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker the black and blue are among the coloured balls, while reds and the cue ball are excluded from that term.

clue.text: Lofty is happy about English victory

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the happy word goes round the other two pieces

parts.note: elated means very happy
V stands for victory, as in the V sign

explanation.surface: Someone tall is pleased with an English win.
explanation.definitionFit: Lofty and elevated both describe something high up or noble in tone.

clue.text: Touching uncertainty in defence

parts.note: re means concerning or touching on
doubt is uncertainty

explanation.surface: A moving lack of certainty when defending oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: A redoubt is a small fortification, part of a defensive position.

clue.text: Poet admitting holding up branch

indicators.note: in a down clue, holding up means supporting from above, so the branch letters sit on top

parts.note: Br is an abbreviation for branch
owning means admitting or confessing, as in owning up

explanation.surface: A poet confessing while propping up a tree limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Browning, and Elizabeth Barrett Browning, were Victorian poets.

clue.text: Compensate for soldiers' exploit

parts.note: the RE, the Royal Engineers, are a British army corps
a coup is a notable feat or exploit

explanation.surface: Making up for the troops' daring deed.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoup a loss is to make it good, compensating for it.

clue.text: Cloth requires money, nothing more

parts.note: cash is money
mere means nothing more than, as in a mere child

explanation.surface: Fabric costs money and nothing else.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is a fine soft wool fabric made from goat hair.

clue.text: Slater set off alarms

indicators.note: set off means triggered but also displaced, so the letters of Slater are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A roofer triggered the warning bells.
explanation.definitionFit: Alerts are warnings or alarms raised to signal danger.

clue.text: A good shot in Montana provides grub

indicators.note: in puts the three pieces inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: MT is the postal abbreviation for Montana
a go is an attempt or shot

explanation.surface: A fine bit of shooting in Montana puts food on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grub' suggests food, but here it is a larva.
explanation.definitionFit: A maggot is the larva of a fly, a kind of grub.

clue.text: Destruction of plant border

parts.note: may is hawthorn, a flowering plant
a hem is the edge or border of cloth

explanation.surface: Ruin of a garden's flower bed edging.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem is violent disorder and havoc, wanton destruction.

clue.text: G-man turns passionate? That's insulting!

indicators.note: turns means turns round, so the G-man word is read backwards

parts.note: a fed is an FBI agent, known as a G-man
amatory means relating to sexual love, so passionate

explanation.surface: An FBI agent becomes amorous, which is offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Defamatory remarks damage someone's good name, so they are insulting.

clue.text: Food available for fellows going to university

parts.note: men are fellows

explanation.surface: Something to eat for chaps going off to college.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu lists the dishes on offer at a restaurant, the food on hand.

clue.text: Service graduate's Sierra

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts graduate; with the possessive it gives MA's
Sierra is S in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A church service held in some graduate's mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: Mass is the Eucharistic church service.

clue.text: Staff holding revolutionary leader fast

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the staff word wraps round the letter

parts.note: a stave is a staff or stick

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Employees keep a radical's chief quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like speed, but means go without food.
explanation.definitionFit: To starve is to go without food, the same as to fast.

clue.text: Game that's hard for rustic to grasp

indicators.note: to grasp means to hold within, so the rustic word contains the hard letter

parts.note: a peasant is a country labourer
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Hunting is tough for a country dweller to grasp.
explanation.definitionFit: Pheasants are game birds shot for sport.
